digest.component_or_area: complexity baseline gate and maintenance tooling
propositions: Ruff C901 diagnostics against src/rebar production code exceed threshold 15; live census must be captured in a committed baseline JSON with one ceiling entry per finding, keyed by repository-relative path and AST-qualified function name.

The complexity wrapper (check_complexity_baseline.py) accepts Ruff return codes 0 and 1 as normal diagnostic operation and exits zero only when all current findings are at or below their recorded ceilings, rejecting new or increased complexity debt while allowing stale debt reductions.

Maintenance mode (--update-stale) can only lower existing ceilings or remove entries with no current diagnostic; it refuses to write if new or increased debt exists, using atomic_write to guarantee target integrity on write/replace failure.

The baseline JSON schema enforces schema_version 1, valid UTF-8, no duplicates, sorted ceiling keys in form path::qualified-symbol, and ceiling values strictly greater than 15; the loader rejects malformed data before comparison.

Symbol identity derives from Python AST FunctionDef and AsyncFunctionDef nodes with dot-joined class/function ancestry; duplicate same-qualified-key diagnostics, lambdas without definitions, and unknown AST ambiguities fail normalization rather than overwriting.

The make lint target invokes the complexity wrapper over src/rebar (shrink-only production scope) while retaining existing Ruff and format checks over src and tests; committed baseline reflects the current origin/main C901 census as of the latest measured state.
